title: How early should you arrive at Aberdeen Airport?
author: Matt
cover_image_alt: Runway approach lights and their orange and white posts glowing in a hazy sunrise
intro: About two hours before an international flight and 90 minutes to two hours for a UK flight is the usual advice at Aberdeen. Here's how to work out your timing, with security, drop-off and the Jet 727 bus.
seo_description: About 2 hours before international flights and 90 minutes to 2 hours for UK flights. Aberdeen security, the 100ml liquids rule, drop-off and the 727 bus.

sections.heading: The short answer
sections.text:
- **Abroad, bags to drop:** about 2 hours
- **UK flight, hand luggage:** 90 minutes
- **Early mornings:** add 30 minutes
- **School holidays:** add 30 minutes

This is the timing most airlines and travel guides suggest for Aberdeen, checked in October 2026. Your airline's bag drop and gate deadlines are the ones that count, and they're on your booking. Procedures change, so check the airport's and the airline's current advice before you travel.

sections.heading: Why Aberdeen is usually quick
sections.text:
Aberdeen International Airport, at Dyce, has a single terminal for passenger flights, so there's no terminal to choose and the walk from the door to security is short. Most of the year it's a calm airport, and many regulars who fly to London for work arrive well under two hours before.

That doesn't hold on every flight. The airport gets busy in waves, with several departures leaving at once in the early morning, and the Scottish school holidays bring a rush of families with bags to drop. Summer is busiest, when Ryanair, TUI and the other sun flights run alongside the city and business routes. If you only fly from Aberdeen now and then, two hours is the safe default. Cut it down only when you're travelling light on a quiet midweek flight.

sections.heading: How early for your flight
sections.text:
| Trip | Flight | Arrive |
| --- | --- | --- |
| London or Manchester, hand luggage only | Midweek, mid-morning | **About 90 minutes** before |
| City break, bags to drop | Friday evening | **About 2 hours** before |
| Sun holiday, bags to drop | 6am in July | **2½ hours** before |
| Flight via Amsterdam or Heathrow | Any time | **2 hours** before |

On a connecting trip through Amsterdam with KLM or Heathrow with British Airways, check in for the whole journey at Aberdeen and your bag goes all the way through. The airline will rebook you if the first flight is late, as long as it's all on one ticket.

sections.heading: Security and liquids
sections.text:
Aberdeen has new-generation security scanners, and in 2024 it was one of the first UK airports to relax the liquids rules. That didn't last. The government brought back the 100ml limit at these airports in June 2024, and Aberdeen's own security page still says liquids must be in containers of 100ml or less, checked in October 2026.

Watch out: some UK airports now allow up to 2 litres, so a friend's advice from Edinburgh or Heathrow may not apply at Aberdeen. Pack your liquids to 100ml in a clear bag, and you'll be fine at both ends of the trip.

Follow the signs and the staff on whether to take liquids and laptops out of your bag, as it can depend on the lane you're in.

sections.heading: Bag drop and the gate
sections.text:
If you have a bag to check in, work back from the bag drop deadline, not the departure time. Most airlines close bag drop somewhere between 40 and 60 minutes before departure, and the exact time is on your booking. Budget airlines don't make exceptions, even if the plane is still at the gate.

The gate closes before the published departure time too, often 20 to 30 minutes before. Aberdeen's gates are close together, but don't leave it until the last call.

Tip: check in online as soon as it opens. With hand luggage only and a boarding pass on your phone, you can go straight to security.

sections.heading: Winter mornings
sections.image_alt: A passenger jet covered in snow at night, with passengers climbing the steps to board
sections.image_caption: On frosty mornings, de-icing can hold your plane on the stand for a while.
sections.text:
North-east Scotland gets frost, fog and the odd heavy snowfall between November and March. On a cold morning, planes may need de-icing before take-off, and the roads to Dyce can be slow, especially from Aberdeenshire.

Allow extra time for the drive or the bus rather than at the airport itself. If the weather turns, check your flight status before you leave home.

sections.heading: Getting there and dropping off
sections.image_alt: Inside Aberdeen railway station, with a glass roof, a Welcome to Aberdeen sign and travellers with suitcases
sections.image_caption: The 727 bus leaves from Union Square, next to Aberdeen railway station.
sections.text:
- **By bus:** the Stagecoach **Jet 727** runs between Union Square bus station, next to the railway station, and the front of the terminal. It runs from early in the morning until late at night, and you can buy a ticket in the Stagecoach app. Check the timetable for the hour you need.
- **By train:** Dyce railway station is a short taxi or bus ride from the terminal, handy if you're coming from Inverness or the north.
- **Drop-off:** there's a charge for the express drop-off zone outside the terminal, reported at £7 in 2026. Check the airport's website for the current price and any free drop-off area in the long stay car park.
- **Parking:** booking ahead online is almost always cheaper than paying on the day.

Aberdeen is about 7 miles from the city centre, but allow for traffic on the A96 and around Dyce at rush hour.

sections.heading: Five ways to make the airport easier
sections.text:
- **Check in online** as soon as it opens.
- **Pack liquids to 100ml**, whatever other airports allow.
- **Work back from your bag drop deadline**, not the departure time.
- **Book parking in advance** if you're driving.
- **Allow extra time in winter** for the roads, not the queues.

sections.heading: Where could you go from Aberdeen?
sections.text:
Aberdeen's direct routes include [Amsterdam](/destinations/amsterdam) and [Paris](/destinations/paris) all year, and summer flights to [Málaga](/destinations/malaga), the [Algarve](/destinations/algarve) and [Kraków](/destinations/krakow). easyJet is adding [Barcelona](/destinations/barcelona) and [Mallorca](/destinations/mallorca) in 2027. Our guide to [where you can fly direct from Aberdeen](/blog/where-can-you-fly-direct-from-aberdeen-airport) has the full list.

For more ideas, browse the [city breaks](/destinations/city-breaks) page. If your family can't agree, read our guide to [deciding where to go on holiday](/how-to-decide-where-to-go-on-holiday), or put everyone's picks into a draw.

faqs.question: How early should I get to Aberdeen Airport?
faqs.answer: About two hours before an international flight, especially with a bag to drop. For a UK flight with hand luggage only, 90 minutes is usually enough. Allow more on early mornings and in the school holidays.

faqs.question: Is the 100ml liquids rule still in place at Aberdeen Airport?
faqs.answer: Yes. Aberdeen's security page says liquids must be in containers of 100ml or less, checked in October 2026. Some other UK airports allow more, so check before you pack.

faqs.question: How do you get from Aberdeen city centre to the airport?
faqs.answer: The Stagecoach Jet 727 bus runs from Union Square bus station, next to the railway station, to the front of the terminal. A taxi or a lift takes about 20 to 30 minutes, depending on traffic.

faqs.question: Does Aberdeen Airport have more than one terminal?
faqs.answer: No. All passenger flights use the same terminal, so there's no terminal to choose.
